extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in nonlinear time series analysis (physics, geosciences, life sciences) who use recurrence plots, cross- and joint-recurrence analysis, and recurrence quantification analysis (RQA)
extracted.subtask_description: Compute and interpret recurrence plots (RP), cross-recurrence (CRP), joint-recurrence (JRP) and recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) measures to characterise dynamics, detect synchronisation, time rescaling, transitions, and nonlinear interrelations in time series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence rate (RR)
rubrics_metrics.description: RR(ε) = (1/N^2) sum_{i,j} R_{i,j}(ε). It measures the density (percent) of recurrence points in the RP and, in the N→∞ limit, the probability a state recurs to its ε-neighbourhood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RR corresponds to the correlation sum (LOI usually excluded). For CRPs RR equals the cross-correlation sum CC2(ε); for JRPs RR equals the joint correlation sum JC2(ε(1),...,ε(n)). Interpret as baseline recurrence density; use when comparing overall recurrence density between data or conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average number of neighbours Nn(ε)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nn(ε) = (1/N) sum_{i,j} R_{i,j}(ε) — the average number of neighbours each point has in its ε-neighbourhood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful diagnostic of neighbourhood size and density; relates directly to RR (RR = Nn/N).

rubrics_metrics.name: Histogram of diagonal lines P(ε,l)
rubrics_metrics.description: P(ε,l) counts the number of diagonal lines of length l in the RP; used as base distribution for many diagonal-based RQA measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute P(l) (omit ε in notation for simplicity). Diagonal-based measures (DET, L, Lmax, ENT_R) are derived from P(l). Careful with sparse histograms if lmin is large.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinism (DET)
rubrics_metrics.description: DET = (sum_{l=lmin}^N l P(l)) / (sum_{l=1}^N l P(l)). It is the ratio of recurrence points that form diagonal lines of at least length lmin to all recurrence points and measures predictability/determinism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude short diagonals due to tangential motion by choosing lmin (similar idea to Theiler window). For lmin=1, DET=1. If lmin too large P(l) becomes sparse and DET reliability decreases. DET decreases for stochastic/weakly correlated processes and increases for deterministic processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average diagonal line length (L)
rubrics_metrics.description: L = (sum_{l=lmin}^N l P(l)) / (sum_{l=lmin}^N P(l)). The mean length of diagonal structures; interpretable as the mean prediction time (how long two trajectory segments stay close).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with appropriate lmin. Longer L indicates slower divergence of nearby trajectories; compare across conditions or parameter sweeps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longest diagonal line (Lmax) and divergence (DIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lmax = max_{i} l_i (longest diagonal length). DIV = 1 / Lmax. These relate to exponential divergence and can be used as estimators for Lyapunov-like behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eckmann et al. related diagonal lengths to the largest positive Lyapunov exponent, but relationship is not simple. Lmax can be used to estimate K2 entropy / lower bound of sum of positive Lyapunov exponents with caution. Use supplemental methods for rigorous Lyapunov estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entropy of diagonal lengths (ENT_R)
rubrics_metrics.description: ENT_R = - sum_{l=lmin} p(l) ln p(l), where p(l)=P(l)/N_l (probability of a diagonal of length l). Reflects complexity of diagonal-length distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low ENT_R for uncorrelated noise; higher values indicate more complex distributions of diagonal lengths. Compute with same lmin used for other diagonal measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: τ-wise (diagonal-parallel) measures: RR_τ, DET_τ, L_τ
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute RR, DET, L for each diagonal at distance τ from the main diagonal (parallel lines). RR_τ is the τ-recurrence rate (generalised autocorrelation), DET_τ the τ-determinism, L_τ the τ-average diagonal length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RR_τ interpretable as probability of recurrence after τ time steps and generalised autocorrelation (works in phase space, not just scalar observables). Use RR_τ, DET_τ, L_τ to detect UPOs, non-stationarity, synchronisation, and to select Theiler window. For CRPs, RR_τ reveals similar states between systems with delay τ; high DET_τ, L_τ indicate long time spans of similarity. Validity increases with RP size N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry and asymmetry measures Q(τ) and q(τ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Q(τ) = (RR_τ + RR_{-τ})/2 measures symmetry; q(τ) = RR_τ / RR_{-τ} measures asymmetry between positive and negative delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use on small τ-range to quantify interrelations and determine which system leads (e.g., peaks in Q indicate synchronisation after a lag; sign of q indicates leader). Similar concept to event synchronisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive/negative CRP decomposition and composite measures (RR^+, RR^-, RR^c, DET^c, L^c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute CRPs for positive-linked (CR^+) and negative-linked (CR^-) relations (e.g. using CR^- to detect anticorrelation). Composite τ-measures combine positive and negative contributions: RR^c_τ = (1/N) sum_k (CR^+_{i,j} - CR^-_{i,j})_{j-i=k}, DET^c_τ = DET^+_τ - DET^-_τ, L^c_τ = L^+_τ - L^-_τ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composite measures provide intuitive representation of positive vs negative relations, akin to time-dependent cross-correlation, but are unsuitable if even-function investigation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trend (TREND)
rubrics_metrics.description: TREND = linear regression coefficient of recurrence point density RR_τ of diagonals vs distance τ (computed excluding RP edges). It quantifies non-stationarity and drift in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose truncation size Ñ < N to avoid edge effects. For noise N - Ñ > 10 may suffice; for auto-correlated systems use much larger Ñ (≈10× auto-correlation time). TREND depends strongly on sliding window size when using time-dependent RQA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratio (RATIO = DET / RR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratio defined as DET divided by RR (formulas based on P(l) given). Heuristically used to uncover transitions where RR decreases but DET remains (e.g., dynamical transitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for detecting qualitative transitions in physiology/time series. Interpret with caution and alongside other measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical-line histogram P(v) and laminarity (LAM)
rubrics_metrics.description: P(v) counts vertical lines of length v. Laminarity LAM = (sum_{v=vmin} v P(v)) / (sum_{v=1} v P(v)) is the ratio of recurrence points forming vertical structures of at least vmin to all recurrence points; indicates laminar states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose vmin to reduce tangential-motion influence (vmin=2 appropriate for maps). LAM increases when laminar/intermittent behaviour present and decreases when single isolated points dominate. Periodic dynamics yield zero vertical measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trapping time (TT)
rubrics_metrics.description: TT = (sum_{v=vmin} v P(v)) / (sum_{v=vmin} P(v)). The average length of vertical structures; estimates mean time system remains trapped in a specific state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires appropriate vmin selection. TT and LAM are sensitive to intermittency and helpful to detect chaos–chaos transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum vertical line length (Vmax)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vmax = max_{v} v (maximal vertical line length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to Lmax for diagonals; large Vmax indicates long laminar episodes (useful to detect crises, band merging, intermittency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of diagonal- vs vertical-based measures for different transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagonal-based measures (DET, L, Lmax) detect periodic–chaos/chaos–periodic transitions and are sensitive to predictability; vertical-based measures (LAM, TT, Vmax) detect chaos–chaos transitions, intermittency, and laminar states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare both families across parameter sweeps to identify different types of transitions (e.g., logistic map examples showed diagonal measures highlight order–chaos transitions, vertical measures highlight chaos–chaos transitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of lmin and vmin relative to auto-correlation / tangential motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower limits lmin (for diagonals) and vmin (for verticals) should be chosen to exclude tangential-motion artefacts and false short lines; lmin should be of order of the auto-correlation time; vmin = 2 for maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If chosen too small, tangential motion inflates measures; too large leads to sparse statistics. Use diagonal-wise measures RR_τ to help set Theiler window and lmin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold selection strategies: fixed epsilon vs fixed recurrence density (FAN) vs fixed number of nearest neighbours
rubrics_metrics.description: RP/CRP/JRP can be computed with a fixed distance threshold ε, with a fixed recurrence density (FAN; constant percent recurrences), or by using a fixed number of nearest neighbours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed ε preserves physical scale but may be inappropriate for comparing systems with different measures or for noisy/short non-stationary data. Using fixed recurrence density (FAN) ensures comparable densities across RPs. For short/noisy/nonstationary series, fixed number of neighbours is often preferable. OPRPs or JRPs may also be suitable in these cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-recurrence plot (CRP) vs Joint-recurrence plot (JRP): when to use which
rubrics_metrics.description: CRPs compute differences between vectors of two trajectories in the same phase space (sensitive to rotations/coordinate changes); JRPs consider recurrences in each system's own phase space and mark times when both recur simultaneously (invariant under permutations and affine coordinate changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CRP to study different parts of the same system or the same process under different physical/mechanical transformations (e.g., borehole cores, time rescaling) and to detect time-rescaling via a bowed LOS. Use JRP to study interacting but physically different systems where phase spaces differ (detect inter-system synchronisation/adaptation). CRP cannot meaningfully compare vectors with different physical units/dimensions; JRP preserves individual phase spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line of identity (LOI), Line of synchronisation (LOS), and slope/time transformation interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: For identical trajectories CRP equals RP with a main black diagonal (LOI). Slight amplitude modification disrupts LOI to form LOS. Local slope of diagonal lines corresponds to local time-axis transformation between trajectories; bowed LOS indicates nonlinear time rescaling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve LOS from CRP to determine non-parametric time-transfer function t = φ(t'). Use LOS slope/displacement to detect time shifts, dilations/compressions. If only stretched/compressed in time, LOS is continuous but not slope one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed joint recurrence matrix JR_{i,j}(ε_x, ε_y, τ)
rubrics_metrics.description: JR_{i,j}(ε_x, ε_y, τ) = R^x_{i,j}(ε_x) R^y_{i+τ,j+τ}(ε_y). A delayed JRP considering recurrences offset by τ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for analysing interacting delayed systems (lag synchronisation) and systems with feedback. Can be used to study lagged joint recurrences between systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariant properties and limitations: rotation, affine transformations, and time transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: JRP is invariant under permutation of coordinates and affine transformations; CRP is not invariant under rotations of one system (CRP changes). CRP can detect time parametrisation differences via bowed LOS; JRP cannot detect time transformations if recurrence structures differ in time-scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose analysis type based on whether preserving each system's phase space and invariance to coordinate transforms matters, or whether detecting time-rescaling and local time mappings is the objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter choices and embedding advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding may or may not be necessary (maps often need no embedding; m=1 suffices), but embedding choices (dimension m, delay τ) affect RPs. Threshold choices (e.g., ε = 10% of standard deviation in examples) affect recurrence density and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For maps embedding not necessary but sometimes used for comparability. Smaller ε increases sensitivity to small variations but reduces recurrence density and statistical reliability. Choose parameters considering data length and desired sensitivity; test robustness across reasonable ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical validation and significance estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess significance of RQA/CRP/JRP findings via ensemble methods (e.g., many realisations or surrogates) and use distribution margins (e.g., 2σ bands) to judge significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 500 realisations of an AR model used to estimate distributions of measures; 2σ margins identify significant peaks in RR_τ or L_τ. Statistical reliability increases with RP size (data length).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-dependent (sliding-window) RQA and window-size dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute RQA measures in moving sub-matrices along the LOI to obtain time-dependent behaviour of RQA variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sliding-window results (e.g., TREND) depend strongly on window size; choose window length relative to auto-correlation and time scales of interest. Exclude edges when computing trend or diagonal-wise measures to avoid bias.
